decision.recommended_plan: No conflict exists between the cost and retention recommendations for this population. The retention agent flagged zero employees as critical -- despite three individuals (NYX-001, NYX-007, NYX-013) being underwater on compa-ratio (0.37, 0.76, 0.77 respectively) and NYX-001 carrying a large retention award (184,263.33 USD), the retention agent's role-scope analysis concluded that none of the three occupy broad, senior, or hard-to-replace positions, so none are designated critical-to-retain. Since there is no critical employee for whom a funding delay would pose a retention risk, the cost agent's phasing recommendation (splitting the 389,723.47 USD day-one gap evenly into two phases of 194,861.73 USD each, driven mainly by NYX-001's outsized 216,660.68 USD gap) can proceed without creating any underwater-critical exposure during the unfunded interim period. Recommended plan: adopt the cost agent's phased schedule as proposed -- phase 1: 194,861.73 USD / phase 2: 194,861.73 USD for cost gaps, and correspondingly phase 1: 130,476.07 USD / phase 2: 130,476.07 USD for retention awards -- since both agents' figures already phase on the same [0.5, 0.5] schedule and there is no employee whose criticality would be compromised by that delay. This is a case of genuine agreement, not a compromise: cost's phasing rationale (aggregate budget smoothing) and retention's assessment (no one flagged critical) simply do not intersect in a way that produces tension.
